title: Sin
lead: Sin in the Bible is more than breaking a rule. The Hebrew Bible has several words for it: chet, missing the mark; avon, a twisting and the guilt it brings; pesha, rebellion. The New Testament's hamartia also means missing the mark, and Paul speaks of it as a power that rules people. The Bible's remedies include confession, sacrifice, forgiveness, and, for Paul, the cross.

sections.h: Words for sin in the Old Testament
sections.b: Chet (to miss, to go wrong) is the commonest word. Avon (to bend) names both the wrong and its guilt. Pesha (to rebel) names a break with a ruler or a covenant. Leviticus distinguishes sins committed in error from sins committed "with a high hand" (Numbers 15:30). Psalm 51 uses all three words.

Jesus calls people to repent and forgives sins. Paul speaks of sin as a power that entered the world and rules (Romans 5:12; 6:14). John says that if we say we have no sin we deceive ourselves (1 John 1:8). The churches differ on how sin is passed on (see original sin) and on how far it harms human nature.
